title: Finite-field internal Hom from a finite local system
statement: Let $A$ be a finite field and $S$ a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Use ordinary uncompleted derived categories of module sheaves over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathcal B_A(T)$ for the complexes whose cohomology [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] vanishes outside a finite interval and is constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]: there is a finite constructible locally closed stratification on which each cohomology sheaf is pro-étale locally constant with finite-dimensional $A$-module values. Let $L$ be an $A_S$-module sheaf admitting a pro-étale covering on each member of which it is a constant finite-dimensional $A$-module [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. For integers $a\le b$ and $N\in\mathcal B_A(S)$ with $H^r(N)=0$ outside $[a,b]$, the ambient ringed-site $R\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(L[0],N)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] belongs to $\mathcal B_A(S)$ and has cohomology zero outside the same interval $[a,b]$. More precisely, with $L^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(L,A_S)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom], there are natural isomorphisms $H^rR\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(L,N)\cong L^\vee\otimes_{A_S}H^r(N)$ for all $r$, with sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

proof.text: Choose finite bases of the local coefficient modules and apply the additive constant-module sheafification functor to obtain finite free slice models. The independent-universe slice-Hom comparison shows that the dual has the same finite models. Reuse the proved scalar evaluation and its two naturality lemmas from the bounded-evaluation assembly module. Compare its presheaf map with the dual-basis evaluation after braiding. The dual-basis expansion proves local bijectivity, and module sheafification makes the evaluation a sheaf isomorphism. The monoidal unit here is the recorded structure sheaf, as in the original target.

source.place: Finite-free evaluation (0FNY), exact Hom, and functorial K-injective computation (08J7).

proof.text: The finite-free evaluation isomorphism identifies internal Hom from a finite locally free source with tensor by its dual. Transport colimit preservation from the tensor-Hom adjunction through this isomorphism; obtain limit preservation from the same adjunction with the original source. Preservation of binary products gives additivity, so internal Hom is exact.

source.place: Finite-free evaluation (0FNY), exact Hom, and functorial K-injective computation (08J7).

proof.text: The Hom complex with a degree-zero single source projects isomorphically to its degree-zero source factor; all other product factors have zero source. The product universal property and the projection formula verify the differential and naturality. Exact Hom commutes naturally with homology. Use the stated functorial K-injective existence theorem to obtain a replacement functor and its augmentation with their properties. Compute derived Hom on this replacement, compose these comparisons, cancel its homology quasi-isomorphism, and descend the natural isomorphism through identity times the derived localization. Compose with inverse evaluation.

proof.text: Over a finite field a finite-dimensional module is a finite set. The proved constant-scalar comparison identifies finite local intrinsic module models with finite locally constant module-valued sheaves. Transport to the intrinsic module equivalence and apply the proved general constructible tensor helper of the finite-line tensor module. Transfer back to conclude constructibility of the dual tensor each constructible cohomology sheaf.

proof.text: Transport constructibility across the natural dual-tensor cohomology isomorphism. Outside the given interval the cohomology sheaf is zero; additive Hom preserves zero objects, so the cohomology formula gives zero in precisely the same interval. Restrict the natural isomorphism to the full subcategory of admissible pairs. Empty sites, zero rank and a single-degree interval require no exceptions.
